title: This video is a JSON file | Every single shot in my game's trailers is a line of JSON that the sim checks before filming
author: HELLEVATOROP
selftext:
How it works:

1. A shot is a render spec in a JSON file: the hero, the boss, where everyone stands, and every input with frame waits between them ("do=wait150,236L,wait90,...").

2. Before anything is filmed, the spec is played through the game's deterministic sim (fixed 60 Hz, seeded). Every attack has to take HP off its target. If one whiffs, the build stops and prints where everyone was.

3. The cut is JSON too. Each cut says which action it's built around and which beat its hit lands on, and the tool slices the shot so that hit frame lands on that beat of the 126 bpm score.

4. One command films it in headless Chrome, checks the film's hit frames against the sim's (the same frames, or it stops), draws the title cards, renders the score offline, and cuts every language and shape with ffmpeg.

I did this because an early Japanese ad of ours had a special that visibly whiffed the boss. Now a shot that doesn't land can't make it into a video, and moving a cut is a one-number edit instead of a re-record.

The AI part: the agents write and fix the specs from my notes ("land the kill on the downbeat", "zoom in, put the text in the empty space"), and the check is what stops them shipping a shot that misses.

Happy to go into any part of it if you have questions on how the pipeline works, it has made marketing so much better its unbelievable.
